title: The Last Protocol Again
premise: Xanthe Winterbourne has spent eleven years alone tending the Svalbard-9 seed vault and its mysterious beacon, content to be forgotten by the interplanetary war between Earth's Concord and the Belt Collective. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, the beacon activates with a message she never wrote — a dead-man's switch left by her predecessor revealing that the war's opening atrocity was staged by Concord hardliners. Hunted by Concord agents who want the truth buried and befriended by a defecting Belt pilot who needs it broadcast, Xanthe must carry the message to the neutral relay at Ceres. In the end she broadcasts it at terrible personal cost, fracturing both governments but birthing a fragile truce — and finding, in the crew who helped her, the family she never had.
about_author: Mara Almeida is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete communications technology before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she insists the isolation improves her dialogue.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishes her solitary routine at the seed vault: checking seeds, logging weather, maintaining the beacon she believes is decommissioned. When gravity flickers for nine seconds, her instruments go mad and the beacon lights up with an incoming message addressed to 'the Keeper.' Emotional beat: unease breaking through comfortable routine.

chapters.title: The Message That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Xanthe decrypts a partial transmission from Dr. Ilse Varga, her predecessor who died mysteriously years ago — coordinates, a timestamp, and the phrase 'the Cassini lie.' A Concord patrol ship arrives asking strange questions about beacon activity. Emotional beat: dread; her invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn how she came to the vault fleeing a Concord tribunal that blamed her for a navigation disaster she didn't cause. Her sympathy for the falsely accused is established. Emotional beat: melancholy resolve — she knows what it means to be scapegoated.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Fell
chapters.summary: Belt pilot Odile Ferreira crash-lands near the vault, pursued by Concord fighters. Xanthe hides her in the seed vaults' cold stacks. Odile is brash, wounded, and carrying half of a matching decryption key. Emotional beat: wary friction between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Cold Storage Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. While repairing Odile's ship, they exchange guarded histories: Odile lost her brother in the Cassini Station attack, the atrocity that started the war. Xanthe realizes Varga's message claims the attack was staged. Emotional beat: grief finding common language.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The two women fully decrypt Varga's message: flight recorder data proving Cassini was destroyed by Concord weapons, not Belt saboteurs. The message must reach the neutral relay at Ceres within nineteen days or it self-erases. Emotional beat: vertigo — the weight of a war-ending secret.

chapters.title: Concord Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Concord agent Captain Renn Hale boards the vault under diplomatic pretense, probing for the message. Xanthe performs innocence while Odile hides meters away. Hale leaves a tracker behind. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Xanthe discovers she can lie well.

chapters.title: Leaving the Garden
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She seals the vault, sets the beacon to a decoy loop, and abandons the only home she has known for a decade. Saying goodbye to the seed vault is like leaving a grave and a nursery at once. Emotional beat: severance and terror-fueled purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Transit toward Ceres aboard the patched-together ship Perihelion. They evade the tracker, discover Hale has flagged them as terrorists, and bicker their way into genuine partnership. Emotional beat: found-family spark — laughter in a cockpit.

chapters.title: Port Meridian
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They dock at a lawless mining station to buy fuel and meet Tovi Okafor, a teenage hacker stowaway who has been living in their cargo hold since Port Meridian. Tovi recognizes Varga's name — his aunt worked with her. Emotional beat: reluctant adoption.

chapters.title: Tovi's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tovi's POV. He reveals Varga sent fragments to three keepers across the system; the other two are dead. The pattern is clear: someone is erasing witnesses. First assassination attempt on the trio via sabotaged air scrubbers. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Hale corners them via commcast, offering amnesty and reinstatement if Xanthe surrenders the message — he hints he too doubts the official story. Odile calls it a trap; Xanthe isn't sure. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth begins to pull apart the crew.

chapters.title: The Gravity Well Gambit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To lose a Concord blockade they slingshot through Jupiter's radiation belts, nearly killing everyone. Tovi's quick thinking saves the ship; Xanthe realizes she'd die for these two strangers. Emotional beat: bonding forged in near-death.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Tovi's POV. A Belt Collective frigate intercepts them — the Belt wants the message too, but plans to edit it into propaganda. Odile is ordered to hand it over by officers she once served. Emotional beat: disillusionment; no government owns the truth.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The crew escapes the frigate by broadcasting a fragment as bait, but Odile is captured in the maneuver. Xanthe must choose: deliver the message alone or mount a rescue. Emotional beat: guilt and the first real fracture in the found family.

chapters.title: The Price of a Prisoner
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, captive. Hale interrogates her, then reveals his own evidence that Concord command ordered the cover-up — he's been building a case for years and needs a witness who can testify credibly. Emotional beat: enemy becoming uneasy ally; trust as a gamble.

chapters.title: Ceres Rising
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Tovi reach Ceres relay with hours to spare, but broadcasting requires relay credentials held by Concord loyalists — and Odile's execution is scheduled as leverage. Emotional beat: ticking-clock desperation; Xanthe refuses to trade a life for a truth.

chapters.title: Everything Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Tovi hijacks the relay while Xanthe trades herself to Hale for Odile — but Hale double-crosses his own command, giving them the credentials. The full message goes out system-wide: every screen, every ship. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The broadcast ignites mutinies in both fleets; hardliners on both sides attempt a final strike on Ceres, which the crews of both navies refuse to execute. Hale arrests his own superiors. Emotional beat: exhausted awe — the war ending not with victory but with shame.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the neutral hearings, Xanthe testifies about her own false conviction years ago; justice outside the law finally reaches inside it. Her record is cleared, but she declines both governments' offers of rank. Emotional beat: vindication without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Seeds for the Returning
chapters.summary: Tovi's POV. The trio returns to Svalbard-9 to reopen the vault, now joined by refugee families seeking honest work. The beacon is repurposed to broadcast open archives instead of secrets. Emotional beat: warmth; the vault becomes a home rather than a hiding place.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Watch
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, closing chapter. One year later: the truce holds, imperfectly. On the vault's observation deck, her chosen family gathers for the anniversary of the nine seconds. She logs one last entry — not a report, but a letter to whoever keeps watch next. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, love stated plainly.
